purpose: Revefenacin is used to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD, which includes conditions like chronic bronchitis and emphysema. It helps open up your airways so you can breathe more easily throughout the day. It is a maintenance medication, meaning you use it every day to keep your breathing under control, not for sudden breathing problems.
how_it_works: Your airways have tiny receptors that, when triggered, cause the muscles around them to tighten and make it hard to breathe. Revefenacin blocks those receptors, which allows the muscles around your airways to relax and open up. This makes it easier for air to flow in and out of your lungs, helping you breathe better all day long.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a runny or stuffy nose, cough, upper respiratory infections like the common cold, headache, and back pain. Some people may notice a dry mouth. These effects are usually mild and tend to go away on their own.
warnings: Do not use revefenacin as a rescue inhaler — it will not work fast enough to treat a sudden attack of breathlessness. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma (increased eye pressure), trouble urinating, or an enlarged prostate, as this medicine can make those conditions worse. If your breathing suddenly gets worse after using it, stop and call your doctor right away. This medication is inhaled using a nebulizer only, so do not swallow or inject it.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one vial (175 micrograms) inhaled through a nebulizer once a day. You simply breathe in the mist through the nebulizer mouthpiece until the treatment is done, which usually takes a few minutes. Always use it at the same time each day to get the best results.
